source.title: Heterogeneous Computing: Goals, Methods, and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: In a heterogeneous computing (HC) environment, meaning a distributed high-performance environment composed of machines with varied computational capabilities interconnected by high-speed links, can one develop machine-independent programming languages with user-specified directives that both compile a given application into efficient code for any machine in the HC suite and also support decomposing the application into tasks and subtasks while determining the computational requirements of those tasks and subtasks?

evidence.quote: Distributed high-performance heterogeneous computing (HC) environments are composed of machines with varied computational capabilities interconnected by high-speed links.

Machine-independent languages with user-specified directives are needed to (1) allow compilation of a given application into efficient code for any machine in the HC suite, (2) aid in decomposing applications into tasks and subtasks, and (3) facilitate determination of task and subtask computational requirements.

accepted.question_text: In a heterogeneous computing environment composed of interconnected machines with different computational capabilities, how can one refine methods for measuring the current loading and status of the machines and network and for estimating task and subtask completion times accurately enough to support effective mapping decisions?

evidence.quote: Distributed high-performance heterogeneous computing (HC) environments are composed of machines with varied computational capabilities interconnected by high-speed links.
Methods must be refined for measuring the loading and status of the machines in the HC suite and the network, and for estimating task and subtask completion times.

accepted.question_text: In a heterogeneous computing environment, how should the uncertainty in estimated parameter values, such as predicted task completion times, be incorporated into the process of mapping tasks and subtasks to machines?

evidence.quote: Distributed high-performance heterogeneous computing (HC) environments are composed of machines with varied computational capabilities interconnected by high-speed links.
Also, the uncertainty present in the estimated parameter values, such as task completion times, should be taken into consideration in determining the mappings.

accepted.question_text: For heterogeneous computing suites, how should application tasks be modeled so that the model correctly handles the difference between tasks that execute once, such as a simulation, and continuously running tasks, such as monitoring and analyzing sensor information?

evidence.quote: Another area of research is that of modeling the application tasks to execute on the HC suites [1,4].
Individual tasks that execute once (e.g., a simulation) have different requirements than continuously-running tasks (e.g., monitoring and analyzing sensor information).

accepted.question_text: In heterogeneous computing applications that are decomposed into tasks and subtasks, what methods can support the feedback communications required among subtasks?

evidence.quote: It is also assumed that some tasks may be further decomposed into two or more communicating subtasks. The subtasks have data dependencies among them, but are able to be assigned to different machines for execution.
Methods for allowing feedback communications among subtasks tasks are necessary.

accepted.question_text: In heterogeneous computing environments that must satisfy quality-of-service requirements such as priority semantics, bandwidth requirements, guaranteed processor time for certain users, or real-time response capabilities, how can all of these quality-of-service components be incorporated into the environment and its mapping and scheduling decisions?

evidence.quote: One of the functions of stage 3 is to be able to use the information from stage 2 to derive the estimated execution time of each task and subtask on each machine in the HC suite (as well as other quality of service (QoS) attributes, such as security level [23]), and the associated inter-machine communication overhead.

Several HC environments have inherent QoS requirements that must be met. For example, these requirements might involve priority semantics, bandwidth requirements, guaranteed processor time for certain users, or real-time response capabilities. Research is being conducted on how to incorporate all of these components into HC environments.

accepted.question_text: For heterogeneous computing suites, what hierarchical scheduling techniques can make it possible to scale the suite up to very large sizes?

evidence.quote: Distributed high-performance heterogeneous computing (HC) environments are composed of machines with varied computational capabilities interconnected by high-speed links.
Hierarchical scheduling techniques are under development to allow for HC suites to be scaled up to very large sizes.

accepted.question_text: In heterogeneous computing environments where centralized control is inadequate, what distributed mapping heuristics can replace centralized ones while still producing effective task-to-machine mappings?

evidence.quote: A key factor in achieving the best performance possible from HC environments is the ability to match (assign) the tasks and subtasks to the machines and schedule (order) the tasks and subtasks on each machine in an effective and efficient manner. The matching and scheduling of tasks and subtasks is defined as a mapping.
Also, in some environments, distributed mapping heuristics (as opposed to centralized ones) are necessary.

accepted.question_text: Given that most operating systems support multi-tasking at the individual processor level, how should heterogeneous computing mapping procedures incorporate multi-tasking, allocate processor time among different tasks, and still leverage multi-tasking together with other quality-of-service requirements?

evidence.quote: Incorporating multi-tasking is an area of ongoing HC research.

Most operating systems support multi-tasking at the individual processor level, but how to incorporate this into the mapping process, allocate processor time among different tasks, and still leverage this capability with other QoS requirements is being investigated.

accepted.question_text: In multi-user, distributed, peer-to-peer heterogeneous computing environments where users execute tasks on other machines, how should the inherent security issues be addressed?

evidence.quote: Distributed high-performance heterogeneous computing (HC) environments are composed of machines with varied computational capabilities interconnected by high-speed links.
Furthermore, the security issues inherent with multi-user, distributed, peer-to-peer environments where users are executing tasks on other machines must be addressed.
